strengths: Addresses real and complementary limitations of pixel-based PVGs (scalability) and linear CBMs (expressivity), with clear motivation and problem formulation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across synthetic (CLEVR-Hans) and large-scale real-world datasets (CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k) with appropriate baselines, metrics, ablations, and multiple random seeds
Demonstrates genuine scalability achievement: PVGs successfully applied to high-dimensional data (ImageNet-1k) with near-perfect soundness (99.94%), where pixel-based alternatives fail (35.06%)
Produces substantially more interpretable explanations at concept level (e.g., 'small metal cube') compared to diffuse pixel-level masks, with convincing qualitative comparisons (Figures 3-4)
Shows framework generality through two concept extractor instantiations (CLIP-based and unsupervised NCB), demonstrating the approach isn't tied to specific extraction methods
Provides extensive reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters in supplementary materials, clear architecture descriptions, and implementation details for all baselines
Honestly discusses limitations including concept extractor dependency, training complexity/instability, and inherited biases from pretrained models
weaknesses: Framework's effectiveness fundamentally depends on concept extractor quality, yet this critical dependency is under-investigated; no analysis of failure modes with degraded/noisy/entangled concepts

Modest practical performance gains undermine significance claims: CIFAR-100 improvements of 7.9% over CBM but -4.6% vs ResNet-18; ImageNet-1k actually performs 1.55% worse than linear CBM despite claimed expressivity benefits

Pixel-MAC baseline comparison questionable: catastrophic failure (15.27% CIFAR-100, 35.06% ImageNet) likely reflects poor hyperparameter tuning (mask size=32 pixels for 224×224 images) rather than fundamental limitations; no ablation studies on Pixel-MAC mask size or optimization

Shortcut mitigation (Q4) lacks mechanistic understanding: improvement is modest (7.40→6.15 gap), mechanism unexplained, and unclear whether benefits come from PVG dynamics or concept extractors simply ignoring spurious correlations

Information-theoretic guarantees from Merlin-Arthur only apply to binary classification, yet paper uses multi-class settings; extension to high-dimensional concept spaces not addressed, making verifiability claims somewhat overstated

Critical ablation missing: no investigation of how much improvement derives from PVG training versus the pretrained concept extractor itself; concept extractors achieve 85.96% (CIFAR-100) vs NCV's 83.32%, suggesting extractors rather than PVG architecture drive performance

Three-agent min-max training complexity acknowledged but not investigated: no convergence analysis, training stability metrics, or computational cost comparison with baselines despite known instability of such optimization
Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines existing components (concept extractors, Merlin-Arthur from Wäldchen et al., PVG framework) without fundamental algorithmic innovation
Rejection class introduced for interpretability guarantees but experiments don't report rejection rates, leaving impact on practical deployment unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem: identifies genuine scalability bottleneck of pixel-based PVGs and proposes sensible concept-space solution

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple datasets (synthetic and real-world), systematic research questions (Q1-Q4), proper statistical reporting (10-20 seeds with means/std), extensive ablations

Honest treatment of theoretical limitations: explicitly acknowledges that Merlin-Arthur guarantees don't directly apply to high-dimensional multi-class setting; clearly states theory serves as qualitative lens not quantitative certification; identifies unvalidated assumptions (AFC, class imbalance, relative success rate)
Scalability demonstrated: Pixel-MAC fails entirely on ImageNet while NCV succeeds; training 1-3 orders faster than Pixel-MAC
Interpretable explanations: Figure 3 convincingly shows concept-level explanations are more human-understandable than pixel masks
Technical execution: clean decomposition into components, practical training procedure with continuous/hard mask switching, detailed experimental methodology
weaknesses: Verifiability claims are overstated: framework provides robustness relative to given concept subsets, not end-to-end correctness; soundness only means trained Morgana cannot fool Arthur (weaker than arbitrary adversarial robustness); explicitly not causal—doesn't prove concepts are sufficient for task

Theoretical analysis largely unrealized: authors explicitly do NOT estimate class-wise error metrics (ε_c, ε_s), AFC (κ), or relative success rate (α) numerically; assumption that symmetric architectures ensure α≈1 is heuristic only; high-dimensional sparsity makes average precision PrD(M) difficult to estimate from finite samples

Critical dependence on concept extractor quality underexplored: framework success entirely depends on extractor quality, but paper doesn't systematically vary it; CLIP biases acknowledged but not investigated; no guidance provided for practitioners to validate extractor quality

Substantial accuracy-interpretability tradeoff on realistic data: ImageNet 67.04% (NCV) vs 76.01% (ResNet-50) is 9-point gap; on ImageNet nonlinear CBM (69.02%) outperforms NCV (67.04%), questioning added complexity
Weak evidence for shortcut mitigation: Table 2 shows only modest improvements over CBMs (~2-4% reduction in validation-test gap); Q4 claimed as answered affirmatively but improvements are incremental

Pixel-MAC baseline appears inadequately optimized: achieves only 15.27% on CIFAR-100 and 35.06% on ImageNet; unclear if careful hyperparameter tuning was attempted; massive failures suggest possible implementation issues
Limited novelty: components (Merlin-Arthur, concept extractors) are from existing work; contribution is primarily architectural integration rather than fundamental innovation
Q3 (explanations) addressed only qualitatively: no human evaluation; unclear if selected concepts align with domain expertise; only 5/32 concepts shown for ImageNet examples
No code release mentioned: reproducibility depends on external pretrained models
Brief treatment of limitations: Discussion section doesn't adequately address when NCV would/wouldn't be applicable

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning multiple datasets (CLEVR-Hans, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, COCOLogic), concept extractors (NCB, SpLiCE), and baselines with proper ablations and multiple random seeds

Successfully addresses a clear limitation of prior work by scaling PVGs to high-dimensional image classification through concept-level encoding, demonstrating 1-3 orders of magnitude speedup over Pixel-MAC

Simultaneously improves multiple desiderata: competitive/superior completeness, near-perfect soundness, interpretable concept-based explanations, and demonstrates some robustness benefits to spurious correlations

Honest and thorough treatment of limitations—clearly explains in Appendix A.5 when theoretical guarantees don't hold and why, acknowledges dependency on concept extractor quality, and discusses training complexity
Demonstrates that nonlinear classifiers can operate on concepts while maintaining interpretability and verifiable properties, narrowing the interpretability-accuracy gap inherent to linear CBMs
weaknesses: Theoretical guarantees are substantially weaker than initial framing suggests: formal mutual-information bounds are not computed in high-dimensional multi-class settings; completeness/soundness serve as proxies rather than certified guarantees; this limitation should be more prominent earlier than Appendix A.5

Significant accuracy-interpretability tradeoffs remain on realistic datasets: ImageNet-1k gap of ~9% vs ResNet-50 and ~1.5% vs CBM suggests interpretability still comes at substantial cost; these gaps lack thorough analysis

Critical dependency on concept extractor quality is underexplored: no systematic study of how concept entanglement, discovery method, or quality degradation affects NCV performance; CLIP biases inherited but not investigated

Contribution is primarily engineering-focused (combining two existing methods) rather than introducing novel techniques, theoretical insights, or discovery mechanisms; core idea is straightforward once components exist

Shortcut robustness claims are overstated: Table 2 shows inconsistent benefits (NCV's gap at 0% clean data is worse than nonlinear CBM on CLEVR-Hans3), and the mechanism by which PVGs mitigate shortcuts remains unclear

Soundness only guarantees robustness against the trained Morgana adversary rather than worst-case adversaries over concept space; high soundness scores may reflect limited adversary strength rather than fundamental robustness
Soundness is extremely sensitive to hyperparameter γ (Fig. 5): drops from 100% to ~10% as γ decreases, but guidance for practitioners on setting γ across diverse domains is limited
